references.text: Abraham fell on his face and laughed (וַיִּצְחָק) when God promised him a son through Sarah. The same root צחק (to laugh) is used here as in Sarah's exclamation that God has given her laughter.
God commands that the son be named Isaac (יִצְחָק), a name meaning 'he laughs', which directly connects to Sarah's wordplay with צחק in her outburst of joy.
Sarah laughed (וַתִּצְחַק) in unbelief at the promise of a son in her old age. This laughter of doubt is transformed into laughter of joy at Isaac's birth.
When the Lord restored the fortunes of Zion, their mouths were filled with laughter. A parallel theme of God's intervention creating joy and laughter.
Elizabeth's neighbors and relatives rejoiced with her when the Lord had shown her great mercy, paralleling how all who hear about Sarah's birth will laugh with her.
Sarah is mentioned as an example of faith: by faith she received power to conceive a child despite her age, because she trusted in Him who had given the promise.
Direct continuation of the same event: Sarah's denial of her laughter is followed by her affirmation of God's intervention.
Chronological and thematic connection: 18:12 is the action (the laughter), 21:6 is the interpretation (God turned sorrow into joy).
Historical confirmation: 24:36 confirms the fulfillment of the miracle that Sarah celebrates in 21:6.
Thematic parallel: God's gift of a son removes the shame of barrenness for both Sarah and Rachel.
Fulfillment of prophecy: 21:6 is the historical fulfillment of the promise quoted in Rom 9:9.
Thematic parallel: God's comfort (the gift of children) leads to public joy and rejoicing.
